name.basis: The firm's own brand ('TCV' in the site's title and copyright line); the adviser's legal name is TCMI, Inc. (Form ADV, CRD 160389), and the older name Technology Crossover Ventures survives in fund and filing names.

founding_year.basis: The firm's own post of 2025-06-23: 'On June 23, 1995, we closed on TCV 1.' The approach page: 'Since our founding in 1995'.

history.value: TCV was founded in 1995 by Jay Hoag and Rick Kimball, who closed its first fund that June. It backed Netflix, Facebook, Airbnb, Spotify and ByteDance as private companies and often held on after they listed, the crossover in its name. Its largest fund, TCV XI, closed at $4 billion in 2021; it manages $23 billion from Menlo Park, New York and London, and the track record on this page covers its minority stakes only.
history.basis: Founders from Wikipedia (TCV (investment firm): 'founded in 1995 by Richard H. Kimball and Jay Hoag') and the first close from the firm's 30th-anniversary post; the five companies are portfolio rows entered while private (Netflix before its 2002 listing, Facebook, Airbnb, Spotify, ByteDance in 2018); 'crossover' from the TCV XI post ('We lived up to our middle name, crossover, by supporting our portfolio companies throughout their entire lifecycle as private and public companies'); TCV XI at $4 billion from https://www.tcv.com/news/tcv-closes-tcv-xi-at-4-billion/; $23 billion and the three offices from https://www.tcv.com/approach (stats as of 2026-06-30). Moved off the page: the fund ladder before TCV VIII (the 2014 release puts capital raised since inception at nearly $10 billion); the 2021 SPAC TCV Acquisition Corp (liquidated 2023, not a portfolio company); the positions left out of the track record: control positions the firm labels 'majority' (GoDaddy, Travelport, Orbitz, Genesys, ETQ and others; decisions.md D6), purchases of listed shares (D6, delta X1) and single-deal vehicles (TCV Sports, NB Co, Bus Co and others), counted in report.md.

investment_concept.basis: The homepage's title-tag tagline, 'Partners in Growth | TCV' (read 2026-09-29), in sentence case with a closing period; the homepage has no headline (a video hero). Competing line: the meta description 'Partnering with exceptional teams to build category-defining technology companies'.

investment_stage.basis: The firm's own words ('a leading growth equity investor'; Velocity, 2022: 'a $460 million fund geared towards expansion-stage investment opportunities'; VCJ, 2022-01-31: 'With the launch of Velocity, TCV now serves entrepreneurs from Series A all the way to IPO and beyond'), reconciled with the landed entry stages: Growth 132, Series A 6 (Avalor, Legit Security, Nagomi Security, Nourish, tastytrade, Zillow), round not on record 158 (mostly the 1996-2012 book, whose listings carry no round). A growth book with a small Series A sleeve.

investment_geo.basis: Derived from hq_country on the landed base (296 companies; the firm publishes no geography filter): United States 244; Europe 29 (United Kingdom 6, France 5, Germany 5, the Netherlands 3, Finland 2, Sweden 2, and one each in Norway, Poland, Ireland, Denmark, Switzerland and Austria; a London office); Canada 8; Israel 4; India 3; Australia 3; China 3 (two mainland, Hong Kong 1); and one each in Japan and Brazil. Regions with two or more companies are listed.

investment_scope.basis: Derived: the site's four focus areas (Infrastructure Software, Application Software, Fintech & Payments, Consumer/SME; the homepage's sectors list) crosswalk to Data Infrastructure, SaaS, Fintech & Payments and Consumer & Marketplaces; the focus column adds Media, Gaming & Advertising. The five sectors listed each hold at least 18 of the 296 companies (profile.focus_min_companies): SaaS 73, Consumer & Marketplaces 60, Fintech & Payments 42, Data Infrastructure 36, Media, Gaming & Advertising 29. Below the floor: Security 16, Healthcare & Bio 11, AI & Applied AI 9, DevTools & APIs 6, Industrial & Robotics 4; 10 outside the taxonomy (services, consulting, hardware). Five sectors read Generalist.

investment_range.basis: LOWER and UPPER LIMIT: the firm's own range, '$10M - $500M equity investments and flexibility around structure' (approach page, stats as of 2026-06-30). MEDIAN: press- and filing-based, a ROUND-SIZE PROXY and not the firm's cheque: 62 members' notes state the size of the round in which TCV entered; their median is about $75M (25th percentile $42M, 75th $160M; Growth rows $100M, Series A rows $24M), published as $75M. The note parse is approximate (secondaries and rows naming only a valuation are left out; Mambu's EUR 110M converted at about $134M). Wikipedia's '$3 million to $300 million' is older than the firm's own range and is not used.

notable_investments.basis: The five best known of the firm's companies, most recognised first (PRO-152). Also considered: Zillow, Peloton, Revolut, Nubank, Anthropic, Klarna. Expedia and LinkedIn, often named with TCV, were listed purchases and are not portfolio rows (decisions.md D6).

aum.basis: BOTTOM: TCMI, Inc.'s Item 5.F regulatory assets, $22,506,060,259 (Form ADV, CRD 160389, annual amendment of 2026-03-27), which the Section 7.B.(1) gross asset values of its 34 private funds sum to exactly. TOP: the firm's own '$23B assets under management' (https://www.tcv.com/approach, stats as of 2026-06-30). The 2022 Velocity post's '$28 billion ... as of September 30, 2021' is older than both and is not used.

sources.note: Form D filings of 2022 (first sale 2022-06-27) report $0 sold. No closing size has been announced; the ADV of 2026-03-27 carries the XII family (XII, XII (A), XII (B), XII (Lux), XII Member Fund) at $3.87 billion of gross assets, a value and not the commitments.

The firm's own post of 2022-01-31: 'Velocity, a $460 million fund geared towards expansion-stage investment opportunities'. Its Form D filings (first sale 2021-09-10) report $0 sold, so no accession is asserted.
The firm's own post of 2021-01-27: 'the closing of TCV XI, our largest fund to date at $4 billion'. Form D filed 2020 with $0 sold.
TechCrunch, 2019-01-31: TCV closed its tenth fund at $3 billion. Form D filed 2018 with $0 sold.
The Wall Street Journal, 2016-08-01: TCV raised $2.5 billion for its ninth fund. Form D filed 2016 with $0 sold.

The firm's own release of 2014-03-19: 'the closing of TCV VIII, a $2.23 billion fund'. The Form Ds report $1.5725B sold by TCV VIII, L.P., $328.8M by VIII (A) and $69.2M by VIII (B); the release's figure covers all vehicles, so no accession is asserted.
On the ADV of 2026-03-27 (Section 7.B.(1), with TCV VII (A)); it predates electronic Form D and no size is cited here.

funds.basis: The flagship funds from TCV VII and the Velocity fund, with the main L.P. named. TCV's funds file Form D before first close with $0 sold, so every size here is the firm's or the press's announced close and no accession is asserted (TCV VIII's sworn vehicles sum to $1.97 billion against the announced $2.23 billion). Counted here, not listed: the parallel vehicles of each fund ((A), (B), (Lux) SCSp, Member Fund), and the single-deal vehicles (TCV Sports, NB Co, Bus Co, Tru Co, Dev Co, Guardian, Beat Co, Juniper Co, Owl Co, Cedar Co, Flare Co). Funds I to VI (1995 to 2006) predate electronic Form D and carry no cited size; the 2014 release puts capital raised since inception at nearly $10 billion.

hq_location.basis: Principal office on the newest Form ADV: 250 Middlefield Road, Menlo Park, CA (TCV, CRD 160389, Annual Amendment filed 2026-03-27). The firm's site lists Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; London, United Kingdom; the principal office is among them, so the site agrees. Rule (Erik 2026-09-24): the newest Form ADV principal office, unless the firm's own site disagrees, and then the site wins.
